title: How Many Entries Are Smaller
statement:
You get an array nums of small non-negative integers. For each position i, count how many entries of the whole array are strictly smaller than nums[i].

Return the counts as an array in the same order as nums. Equal values are not counted.

examples.why: Each 4 is beaten by 0 and 2. Nothing is below 0. Only the 0 is below 2.
Equal values do not count as smaller.
Entries before or after position i both count, not just the ones after it.

hints: Comparing every pair works but is O(n²). The values are tiny: at most 101 different ones.
Count how often each value appears. How many entries are smaller than v, in terms of those counts?
Turn the counts into a running total: below[v] = count of values 0 … v − 1. Then the answer for nums[i] is below[nums[i]].

explain.intuition:
The answer for an entry depends only on its value, not its position: every 4 in the array gets the same count. And there are only 101 possible values. So count how many times each value occurs, then take a running total: the number of entries smaller than v is the sum of the counts for 0 through v − 1.

That is two passes over the array plus one over 101 buckets, the same idea as counting sort. If the values were not small, sorting a copy and finding each value's first position would give the same answer in O(n log n).
steps: Make count of size 101 and count each value.
Build below[v] = count[0] + … + count[v − 1] as a running sum.
pitfalls: Including the running total up to v itself, which counts equal values (and the entry itself).
Counting only the entries after position i. That is a different, harder problem.
Sorting the input in place and then answering in sorted order. The output must follow the original order.

solutions.title: Compare with every entry
solutions.idea: For each entry, scan the whole array and count smaller values.

solutions.title: Sort a copy, first position
solutions.idea: In a sorted copy, the first index of value v is exactly how many entries are smaller.

solutions.title: Count values, running total
solutions.idea: Bucket the values, prefix-sum the buckets, and read each answer from its value's bucket.

followups: Count only the smaller entries to the right of each position. (Hint: a Fenwick tree or merge sort.)
Values go up to 10⁹. Which of the three solutions still works, and how would you adapt the counting one?
lcTitle: How Many Numbers Are Smaller Than the Current Number
